caption:
Gamma turns a topic, your notes or an old PowerPoint into a finished deck.
The free plan gives you 400 credits once, and they do not refresh.
Here is how to make a deck that holds up, and how to export it.

Would you let AI build your next presentation?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Gamma Help Center, Lead with AI · Photo: Lead with AI
threads_text: Gamma builds a whole deck from a topic or your notes, and the free plan gives you 400 credits once. The trick: write your outline first and paste it in with three dashes between slides, or it invents a deck for you. Would you present slides an AI designed?

slides.headline: How to use *Gamma AI* to make a presentation in minutes

slides.heading: 1. Start from *your own notes*
paras: Type a topic, paste notes or import a PowerPoint, a document or a web link.
When pasting, put three dashes between sections so each one becomes its own slide.

slides.heading: 2. Approve the *plan* first
paras: Gamma's agent asks a few questions and shows a plan before it builds. That is Plan mode, the default.
Express skips the questions. Research reads the web first, costs more and needs Pro.

slides.heading: 3. The free plan is *400 credits*
paras: New accounts get 400 credits once. They do not refresh. Each referral adds 200.
Editing by hand is free, so fix small things yourself instead of asking the AI again.

slides.heading: 4. Export to *PowerPoint*
paras: Click Share, then Export, and choose All cards. You get PDF, PNG or PowerPoint.
Free exports carry a Made by Gamma badge. There is no Word export on any plan.

site_article.headline: How to use Gamma AI to make a presentation in minutes, and what the free plan gets you
site_article.dek: Gamma turns a topic, your notes or an old PowerPoint into a designed deck. The free plan is 400 credits, once, so it pays to start from a good outline.
site_article.summary: Gamma is an AI tool that builds presentations, documents and web pages from a prompt, pasted notes or an imported file. New accounts get 400 credits that do not refresh, and decks export to PDF, PNG or PowerPoint.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Gamma AI to make a presentation in minutes
site_article.seo_description: How to use Gamma AI step by step: Plan, Express and Research modes, pasting your own outline, the 400 free credits and exporting to PowerPoint or PDF.
site_article.answer_summary: Sign up at gamma.app, describe your deck in the prompt bar or paste your own outline with three dashes between slides, approve the plan, edit by hand, then click Share and Export to get a PDF or PowerPoint. Free accounts get 400 credits once.
site_article.hero_alt: A presentation slide deck generated by Gamma, shown in the Gamma editor.

paragraphs.text: How to use Gamma AI comes down to one decision: let it invent the deck, or give it your own outline. Gamma builds presentations, documents and web pages with AI. In the current version, Gamma 5, you start by talking to an AI agent in a prompt bar, and the older one-shot generator is still there under Use classic generator on the dashboard.
The short version: Gamma is fast and its slides look finished. It is weakest at facts and at matching a company template. Use it for a first draft you will check, not a deck you present unread.
How Gamma AI builds a deck: the three modes

Type what you want in the prompt bar on your dashboard. You can add notes, attach files, pick a template or connect other tools. The agent then picks one of three modes from the mode picker. Plan is the default: the agent asks clarifying questions, shows a plan and waits for your approval before it builds. Express skips the questions and the plan for a faster first draft. Research runs deep web research before writing, takes longer, uses more credits, works only together with Plan and needs a Pro plan or higher.

If a question does not matter to you, click Decide for me and the agent chooses. The Images dropdown in the prompt bar lets you ask for Image slides in a presentation or Image pages in a document, and the plus button lets you upload your own pictures. While it builds, a slide grid fills in live.
Step by step: your first deck

paragraphs.title: 1. Write the outline yourself
paragraphs.text: Open a plain text file and list your slides: a title line, then two or three points for each. Put a line with only three dashes (---) between slides. Gamma's help center says each section split this way becomes its own slide.

paragraphs.title: 2. Paste it in and keep your words
paragraphs.text: In the classic generator, click Create New AI and choose Paste. Paste your outline and select Preserve this exact text if you do not want Gamma to rewrite it. If you start in the agent instead, attach the file or paste the outline into the prompt bar and say to keep the wording.

paragraphs.title: 3. Or import what you already have
paragraphs.text: Choose Import to upload a PowerPoint or a document, or enter a web address. Gamma pulls in the content and restyles it. This is the quickest way to give an old deck a new look.

paragraphs.title: 4. Approve the plan, then build
paragraphs.text: In Plan mode, read the plan before you approve it. Changing the plan costs far less effort than fixing ten finished slides.

paragraphs.title: 5. Edit slide by slide
paragraphs.text: Click the sparkle icon in the top left of any slide to change it with AI. On Pro, the sparkle icon in the top right edits several slides at once. Change the look with Theme in the upper right, or ask the agent to Restyle, which keeps your content and changes the design.

Gamma's help center says Paste with three dashes splits text into slides and Preserve this exact text keeps your wording. Lead with AI, in a guide published November 14, 2026, recommends the same route: shape the outline first in a chatbot such as ChatGPT or Claude, paste it in, and use one theme and one image style for the whole deck.

paragraphs.title: A prompt that gets a usable first draft
paragraphs.text:
Make a [number]-slide presentation for [audience] about [topic]. The goal is to [what the audience should do or decide afterward]. Use my notes below as the only source of facts; do not add statistics I did not give you. One idea per slide, short bullet points, a title slide and a final slide with next steps.

[paste your notes]
Gamma AI free plan and credits explained

Every AI action in Gamma costs credits: creating with AI, agent edits, adding cards with AI, trying new layouts and making or editing AI images. Editing by hand is free, and you can keep editing manually when the credits run out. Failed actions and the agent's clarifying questions cost nothing, but a finished action costs credits even if you do not like the result.

New Free users get 400 credits at sign up, and they do not refresh. Each referral earns a Free user 200 more credits, up to 2,000 held at once. Paid plan credits refresh on your billing date; the Plus plan in Gamma's own example comes with 1,500 credits a month, and unused plan credits roll over up to double the monthly amount. Gamma does not publish a fixed cost per slide or per image, but it shows the image cost before you generate.

According to Lead with AI, the Free plan also limits a single prompt to 10 cards and puts Gamma branding on decks, while Plus starts at about $8 per user a month billed yearly, allows up to 20 cards per prompt and removes the branding. Prices change often, so check Gamma's pricing page before paying.
Regenerating a whole deck burns credits fast. Make the outline right before you build, then fix small things by hand.
How to export to PowerPoint, PDF or Google Slides

Click Share in the top right, then Export, or open the three-dot menu and choose Export. Pick All cards in the dropdown, or only the current card may be exported. You can export as PDF, PNG or PowerPoint, and get the deck into Google Slides by uploading the PowerPoint file. Speaker notes come along in PowerPoint and Google Slides. Exports match Present mode, not Edit mode.

On the Free plan, PDF and PowerPoint exports carry a Made by Gamma badge. Upgrading removes it from future exports only. Gamma's help center notes that printing from the browser does not add the badge on any plan. Word export is not supported on any plan, and the mobile app cannot export decks over 150 slides to PowerPoint.
What Gamma is bad at

Gamma does not check facts, so every number and claim in a generated deck is yours to verify. Lead with AI also says it is not the right tool when a deck must follow a strict corporate PowerPoint template, and that much of what Gamma does is now built into PowerPoint, Google Slides and the big chatbots.

That makes Gamma best for decks where speed and a clean look matter more than a house style: a pitch draft, a class presentation, a one-off talk. For anything with numbers, give it your own figures in the outline and read every slide before you share the link.
